chunks: A group from the people of al-Kufah came to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام and said to him, “O Commander of the Faithful, supplicate for us with supplications for seeking rain.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام called al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and said, “O Ḥasan, supplicate.”

Then al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “O Allah, stir up for us the clouds by the opening of the gates, with abundant water and cloud-masses, with pouring and streaming, O Bestower. Give us covering, abundant, delightful rain. Open its closures, make easy its release, and hasten its driving with moist airs into the valleys, O Bestower, with the downpour of water, O Ever-Doer. Give us rain: drops, drizzle, pouring, layered and all-covering, general and comprehensive, abundant, thick, merciful, sprinkling and spreading, vast, sufficient, swift, wholesome, blessed, spreading broadly and striking the wide lands, overflowing, heaped, and brimful. And water our plains and our mountains, our desert-dwellers and our town-dwellers, until by it You make our prices low, and bless by it our estates and our cities. Show us provision present and dearness absent. Āmīn, O Lord of the worlds.”

Then he said to al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, “Supplicate.” So al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said: “O Allah, Giver of good things from their proper places, Sender down of mercies from their sources, and Mover of blessings upon their people: from You is the saving rain, and You are the Help sought for help. We are the sinners and the people of sins, and You are the One from whom forgiveness is sought, the All-Forgiving. There is no god but You. O Allah, send the sky upon us as continuous abundant rain, and give us the saving rain, pouring and plentiful; life-giving rain, vast, ample, streaming, wholesome, fertile, abundant, overflowing, surging and resounding; incessant and sweeping, spreading and widespread, hanging low, general, a deluge, driving rain against rain in force, and from which drops emerge without false lightning and without thunder proving untrue. By it You revive the weak among Your servants and bring to life the dead of Your lands, as a grace upon us from You. Āmīn, O Lord of the worlds.”

Before his speech was completed, Allah poured down water abundantly. Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه was asked, and it was said to him, “O Abā ʿAbdillāh, is this something they were taught?” He said, “Woe to you! Have you not heard the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله where he says: ‘Wisdom has been caused to flow upon the tongue of my Ahl al-Bayt.’”

key_terms.اَلسَّحَابَ: the clouds invoked to bring rain
key_terms.اَلْحِكْمَةُ: wisdom flowing on the tongues of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.اَلْغَفَّارُ: the Oft-Forgiving, a divine name invoked in repentance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the accepted supplications and wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام in salat al-istisqa?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the people of al-Kufah seeking rain through the supplications of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, who asks Imam al-Ḥasan and Imam al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام to invoke Allah. Their eloquent duʿās are immediately answered with rain, and Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه cites this as a sign of the divinely-flowing wisdom upon the tongues of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
